meta.title: Restaurant ERP - Order to Invoice Process Flow (Built & Verified)
meta.subtitle: BOM/Semi-FG split, 2-counter billing, 2-level warehouse, GST + multi-currency + GSTR export, WhatsApp automation

views.label: Full Flow
views.note: Full built-and-verified flow from order to GSTR filing export — 13 detailed steps below, each with a worked example

views.label: BOM & Kitchen Split
views.note: On confirm, the BOM explodes: Kitchen gets a KOT (no price), Billing gets the price, Inventory is deducted — see cards 1-3

views.label: Warehouse & Stock Alerts
views.note: 2-level: Central -> Branch; dispatch is a paper record only, Receive is what actually moves stock — cards 4-6

views.label: Billing, GST & WhatsApp
views.note: 2-counter billing -> multi-currency FX lock -> GST invoice (CGST/SGST/IGST) -> GSTR-1 HSN export -> WhatsApp Thank You — cards 7-11

views.label: WhatsApp Offer Campaign
views.note: Owner creates an offer, WhatsApp broadcasts it to REAL past customers — card 12

cards.title: 1. Order Capture — Waiter Tablet
items: The waiter picks the table/takeaway on their own tablet, adds items from the menu, then taps Confirm Order.
Example: Table T-12, Counter 1 — added 2x Butter Chicken + 1x Garlic Naan and confirmed.

cards.title: 2. BOM Explode Engine — the Dish's Real Recipe
items: Every dish's BOM (Bill of Materials) is recursive: a dish can use a Semi-FG (gravy/sauce/marinade) as an ingredient, and that Semi-FG is itself a small recipe made from raw materials.

Example: Butter Chicken = 1 unit of Gravy (Semi-FG) + 200g Chicken. The Gravy itself is made from Tomato + Butter + Spices — on confirm, the system explodes both levels at once and works out the real raw-material quantity needed.

cards.title: 2b. How Semi-FG Raw Material Is Actually Deducted
items: There is no separate 'batch cooked the gravy today' transaction yet. The system does NOT keep a live stock count for Semi-FG items (no 'how much Gravy is left in the pot' number).

Instead, every time a dish using that Semi-FG is ordered, the system walks the recipe down to raw materials and deducts Tomato/Butter/Spices from the branch's real inventory at that moment — as if the Gravy were made fresh for that one order.

Why this is still correct: over a full day, Total Raw Material Used = Total Dishes Sold × Recipe Ratio either way, so the end-of-day inventory numbers come out right regardless of real kitchen batching. What it does NOT yet track is a literal 'we made 10 litres of Gravy this morning' stock entry — that would be a separate future feature (a true Semi-FG production/batch-stock module) if the kitchen wants to track in-progress batches explicitly.

cards.title: 3. Kitchen KOT + Semi-FG Alert
items: The kitchen only sees a ticket with item + quantity (the KOT) — no price, so kitchen staff are never distracted by billing.
Example: the KOT prints 'Butter Chicken x2, Garlic Naan x1'. If the Gravy's recent consumption rate suggests the batch is running low, the kitchen also gets a 'prep now' alert.

cards.title: 4. Central + Branch Warehouse
items: The Owner sets up one Central warehouse (bulk stock) and each branch gets its own local warehouse.
Example: Central dispatches 50 kg Chicken to Branch B2 — this is a paper record only; B2's actual stock has not changed yet.

cards.title: 5. Receive = the Real Stock Move
items: Dispatch is just a record; branch inventory only changes when the branch confirms Receive.
Example: B2 receives 48 kg (out of 50 dispatched) — B2's inventory now gets +48 kg, and the 2 kg shortfall is recorded separately, never hidden.

cards.title: 6. Auto Stock Deduction + Low Stock Alert
items: The moment an order is confirmed, both raw material and Semi-FG raw-material requirements are deducted from the branch's real inventory. If stock is short, the WHOLE order is rejected (never a partial order).
Example: Chicken stock drops below the 20 kg minimum — the Purchase team gets a Low Stock Alert immediately, before it becomes a shortage.

cards.title: 7. POS Receipt — 2 Billing Counters
items: Each branch has 2 independent billing counters (Counter 1 and Counter 2) that can bill at the same time — no queue during rush hours.
Example: Counter 1 bills a dine-in customer while Counter 2 bills a takeaway customer at the same moment — no conflict between them.

cards.title: 8. GST Invoice — CGST/SGST/IGST Auto-Split
items: One company GSTIN, every branch invoices under it. Same state → CGST+SGST split evenly; different state → full IGST — with an HSN/SAC code on every item.
Example: a ₹300 item at 5% GST — same state: CGST ₹7.50 + SGST ₹7.50; a customer from another state instead pays IGST ₹15.00 in one line.

cards.title: 9. Multi-Currency — NRI / Export Billing
items: Payments can be accepted in a foreign currency; the exchange rate is locked at the moment of SALE — if the rate changes later, that past bill never changes. The GST invoice itself always stays in INR (legal requirement).
Example: a ₹363.20 bill, paid in USD — the receipt shows 'Payable in USD: $4.30 (rate locked at ₹84.50)'. Even if tomorrow's rate becomes ₹85, this bill stays exactly as it was.

cards.title: 10. GSTR-1 HSN Export — Filing Ready
items: The Owner/Accountant picks a date range and branch, and downloads an HSN-wise GST summary CSV in one click — it pastes directly into the GST portal's offline filing tool.

Example: two October orders both have items under HSN 2106 @ 5% — the export merges them into one row: Qty 3, Taxable ₹400, CGST ₹10 + SGST ₹10, Total ₹420. Orders from a branch without GST set up are shown separately as 'excluded' — never silently hidden inside the filing.

cards.title: 11. WhatsApp Thank You Message
items: The moment an order is confirmed, a real Thank You message goes to the customer's WhatsApp (if they gave a number) — fully automatic, no manual step.
Example: 'Hi Rahul! Your order #ORD-4821 is confirmed — Total ₹420. Thank you, see you again! 🙏'

cards.title: 12. WhatsApp Offer Campaign
items: When the Owner creates a new offer, it broadcasts to every REAL customer in one click — the list is not invented, it's only people who actually ordered before and gave their number.
Example: 'Saket Branch: 20% off all starters today! Valid until 31 Oct' — sent to 45 past customers at once, with a live sent/failed count.
